newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL ROUT COSTA RICA AS COPA COMES TO LIFE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL ROUT COSTA RICA AS COPA COMES TO LIFE.

text.p: Brazil overcame their jet-lag to rout Costa Rica 5-0 on Friday in a match that finally brought the Copa America to life.
Ronaldo, who scored twice, and Romario each scored superb goals in the group C match between two of the teams who have brought full-strength squads to the tournament.

Their goals came as Brazil, who flew straight to the Copa America after their game against England in Paris on Tuesday, turned on the style in the second half, after looking jittery in the opening stages.
A free kick by Djalminha and an own goal by Costa Rica captain Ronald Gonzalez had steadied their nerves and given them a 2-0 halftime lead.
The match was refreshing change after the four encounters on the first two days of the tournament, featuring below strength teams, produced three goals between them.
Costa Rica played their part but paid the price for giving Brazil's forwards too much freedom.
They probably caused Brazil goalkeeper Taffarel more problems than England had done, when Brazil won 1-0, but every time one of their attacks broke down they were in danger of conceeding a goal.

The Central Americans, who have been invited to take part in the tournament for the first time, began in lively fashion and were unlucky not to be awarded a penalty in the 10th minute when Jafet Soto went crashing down in the area.

Ronald Gomez missed an excellent chance shortly afterwards when he shot wide from a rebound after Taffarel failed to hold a shot. At this stage, the crowd were chanting "Ole" every time Costa Rica strung a few passes together.
But Brazil struck in the 23rd minute when Djalminha scored from a free kick and 13 minutes later, the unlucky slid a Roberto Carlos cross into his own goal.

A rout began to look likely three minutes into the second half when Ronaldo scored his first. A goal seemed certain from the moment Ronaldo broke clear of a flat Costa Rica defence, which waited in vain for the offside flat and watched helplessly as he walloped the ball past goalkeeper Erick Lonnis.
Ronaldo's special effort came one minute later when he turned the unfortunate Gonzalez one way and then the other before firing the ball past Lonnis.
Eleven mintues later, Romario slipped through a group of defenders and then flicked the ball over Lonnis with the outside of his foot for Brazil's fifth.
Lonnis rallied his players round for a conference after each goal but the meetings got smaller each time Brazil scored.

Romario looked ready to turn on some more trickery but was surprisingly substituted by coach Mario Zagallo 15 minutes from the end. He looked none too happy on leaving the pitch but reluctantly took his place on the bench.
"We found that Brazil are more dangerous when they are annoyed," said Gonzalez. "Brazil got annoyed when the crowd began whistling them early in the game."
